Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 99, verse 1–8:

(p-201) Surat al-Zalzalah (The Earthquake)

There are two opinions concerning it:

The first: it is Madani (revealed in Medina). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, Muqatil, and the majority.

The second: it is Makki (revealed in Mecca). This was said by Ibn Masʿud, Jabir, and ʿAta'.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾, meaning: it will be moved with a violent movement, and that is at the establishment of the Hour. Muqatil said: it will quake from the intensity of the voice of Israfil, until everything upon it is broken by the severity of the quaking, and it will not be still until it throws out what is on its back of mountains, buildings, or trees. Then it will move and convulse, and it will bring forth what is in its interior.

(p-202) Concerning the time of this earthquake there are two opinions.

The first: it will occur in this world, and it is among the minor signs of the Hour. This was said by most of the scholars.

The second: it is the earthquake of the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Kharijah ibn Zayd and others. Al-Farra' said: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to me, saying: I said to al-Kalbi: "What do you think of the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its earthquake﴾?" He said: "This is in the same manner as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and bring you forth as (a) bringing forth﴾ [Nuh: 18]," so the verbal noun was attributed to its agent. You say in speech: "I will certainly give you your gift," meaning a gift. The "zilzal" with a kasra is the verbal noun, and with a fatha it is the noun. Abu al-ʿAliyah, Abu ʿImran, and Abu Hayawah al-Jahdari read "zalzalaha" with a fatha on the zay.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the earth will bring forth its burdens﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: what is in it of the dead. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: its treasures. This was said by ʿAtiyyah. Al-Farra' combined the two opinions, saying: it casts out what is in it of gold, or silver, or the dead.

(p-203) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And man will say, "What is wrong with it?"﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: that it is a generic noun encompassing both the disbeliever and the believer. This is the view of those who held it to be among the signs of the Hour, because when it began, not everyone knew that it was among the signs of the Hour, so some asked others until they became certain.

The second: that it refers specifically to the disbeliever. This is the view of those who held it to be the earthquake of the Resurrection, because the believer has knowledge and so does not ask about it, whereas the disbeliever denies it, since he does not believe in the Resurrection, and therefore he asks.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day it will relate its news﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "On that day" is governed by His saying: ﴿When it is shaken﴾ and ﴿and brings forth﴾. So on that day it will relate its news, meaning it will inform of what was done upon it. In the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Do you know what its news is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its news is that it will bear witness against every male and female servant concerning what they did upon its back: it will say, 'He did such-and-such on such-and-such a day.'"

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾. Al-Farra' said: it relates its news by the inspiration of Allah and His permission to it. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Awha laha" means He inspired to it, and He permitted it to inform of what was done upon it. Abu ʿUbaydah said: "laha" has the meaning of "ilayha" (to it). Al-Ajjaj said:

"He inspired to it the resting place, so it settled."

(p-204) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day mankind will depart in scattered groups﴾, meaning: they will return from the place of reckoning, ﴿in scattered groups﴾, meaning: in separate companies. The people of faith will be apart and the people of disbelief will be apart. ﴿To be shown their deeds﴾. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, ʿAisha, and al-Jahdari read "liyarawa" with a fatha on the ya. Ibn ʿAbbas said: meaning, to see the recompense of their deeds. The meaning is that they will return from the station in groups so that they may take their places from Paradise and Hell. It was said: there is inversion and reordering in the speech, its implied sense being: "It will relate its news, because your Lord has inspired it, so that they may be shown their deeds, on that Day mankind will depart in scattered groups." According to this, they will see what they did of good or evil at the station of presentation.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾. The exegetes said: whoever does in the world an atom's weight of good or evil will see it. Aban, from ʿAsim, read "yurah" with a damma on the ya in both instances. We have already explained the meaning of "dharrah" (atom) in Surat al-Nisa' [4:40]. Concerning the meaning of this seeing there are two opinions.

The first: that he will see it in his record.

The second: that he will see its recompense. Muqatil mentioned that it was revealed concerning two men in Medina: one of them considered it a small matter to give the beggar a morsel of bread or a date, and the other was lax about a minor sin. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this to encourage them toward even a little good and to warn them against even a small evil.
